security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI writes a value to mie (e.g., to enable/disable specific interrupt classes during init, HSM suspend/resume, or SBI handler prologue/epilogue) and assumes the write took effect exactly as written, without reading back to verify. Hardware WARL behavior may silently drop or alter unsupported interrupt-enable bits, causing a mismatch between OpenSBI's expected and actual mie state.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csrw mie, <val> without subsequent csrr mie read-back verification; or save/restore of mie across HSM suspend where the restored value is not validated against the written value
security_spec.summary: mie/mip are WARL — writes may be silently coerced; OpenSBI must read-back verify after mie writes and must not assume save/restore fidelity across HSM suspend/resume

findings.finding: MIE save/restore across hart-wait with no read-back verification. saved_mie is read from CSR before enabling MSIE+MEIE via csr_set, then restored via csr_write without confirming the write took effect. Additionally, csr_set(CSR_MIE, MIP_MSIP | MIP_MEIP) at line 169 ORs bitmask constants into MIE without read-back — if MSIE or MEIE were read-only-zero on a non-conforming platform, IPI wake-up would silently fail and the hart could hang in wfi().

spec_citations.excerpt: The mie register must always be implemented. A bit in mie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending. Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.

findings.finding: Suspend non-retentive MIE save reads CSR_MIE directly into hdata->saved_mie, capturing the actual hardware state including ROZ bits. This is correct because the saved value reflects the hardware's view of MIE, not a software-constructed value.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mie register must always be implemented. Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.

findings.finding: MIE restoration after non-retentive suspend writes hdata->saved_mie via csr_write without reading back to verify. The warm-boot path (fw_base.S:346) reinitializes MIE to 0. While saved_mie was hardware-derived from the same physical hart, the absence of read-back-after-write means a silent WARL drop during restore would go undetected, potentially leaving interrupts disabled that S-mode software expects to be enabled.

spec_citations.excerpt: A bit in mie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending. Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.

findings.finding: SiFive TMC0 HSM stop saves MIE, then uses csr_set(CSR_MIE, MIP_MEIP | MIP_MSIP) to enable wake-up interrupts before power-gating. No read-back verification after csr_set to confirm MEIE/MSIE were actually enabled. On error rollback, csr_write(CSR_MIE, mie) restores the saved value without read-back verification. A silent WARL drop on either path could leave the hart in unexpected interrupt state.

spec_citations.excerpt: Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.

findings.finding: Andes HSM stop writes csr_write(CSR_MIE, 0) then conditionally csr_write(CSR_MIE, MIP_MSIP) for light sleep wake-up. The MIP_MSIP constant is written directly to MIE without reading back to confirm the MSIE bit was actually set. If MSIE is read-only-zero (e.g., on a single-hart system per spec norm:mip_msip_mie_msie_maybe_rdonly0), the core may fail to wake from light sleep.

spec_citations.excerpt: If a system has only one hart, or if a system has multiple harts but software interrupts are not implemented, then mip.MSIP and mie.MSIE may both be read-only zeros.

findings.finding: Warm-boot initialization writes csrw CSR_MIE, zero to disable all interrupts. Writing 0 to MIE is always safe since read-only-zero bits are already 0, and clearing writable bits cannot be WARL-dropped.

spec_citations.excerpt: Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.

findings.finding: Cold boot initialization writes csr_write(CSR_MIE, 0) to disable all interrupts before entering S-mode. Writing 0 to MIE is always safe — ROZ bits are already 0 and writable bits are correctly cleared.

spec_citations.excerpt: Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.

findings.finding: Andes system suspend writes csr_write(CSR_MIE, 0) to prevent unexpected WFI exit. Writing 0 to MIE is always safe.

spec_citations.excerpt: Bits of mie that are not writable must be read-only zero.
